changes.after: The 2.25-mile LAX people mover, 99% complete but years late, had to enter passenger service by its 8 December 2026 longstop date; contractor LINXS now says service could begin on 6 January 2027, with "no assurances" it will not slip again.
changes.before: The 2.25-mile LAX people mover, 99% complete but years late, must enter passenger service by its project longstop date of 8 December 2026 or its developer LINXS risks a technical default on $1.2 billion of bonds.

changes.after:
• In a 16 September disclosure filing, LINXS said it will need time beyond the 8 December completion deadline; if all goes well the train could be running by 6 January 2027, though "there can be no assurances" the date will not slip further
  • Before opening, the train must pass 30 consecutive days of testing, an independent review and an assessment by Los Angeles World Airports, and a utility agreement with the Los Angeles Department of Water and Power must be completed
  • Recent testing was paused twice to fix track components that "accommodate movement resulting from temperature changes, seismic activity and normal structural behavior"
  • Bondholders agreed to push the lender longstop date on the SkyLink bonds back to December, lining it up with the construction longstop and averting a technical default that would have been triggered in October
  • Fitch's Seth Lehman said the best case is a 30-day commissioning test starting by the end of September, a utility agreement and public service beginning by December 8, "but it's very tight"; a delay beyond December would need LAWA's consent
  • The project is more than 99% complete, and a dispute over the interconnection agreement with the Los Angeles Department of Water and Power, which LAX has not signed, remains; the developer has money for debt service only into early to mid-2027
  • The California Municipal Finance Authority issued $1.2 billion of bonds for LINXS in 2018; Fitch cut them to BB in July 2026 after LINXS sued the city on July 9
  • Construction was first due in March 2023; systems demonstration testing began on April 21, 2026, and the project longstop date is December 8, 2026
  • An August 2026 report had the $3.34 billion system targeting passenger service in October 2026

Notable features

  • A 2.25-mile driverless train with six stations linking the terminals, the LAX/Metro Transit Center and the Rental Car Center

changes.after:
• Leaks out of China claim AMD "could be prepping a 12nm Polaris 30 GPU to be launched before the end of 2018"; the leak was posted on the Chinese site ChipHell and is attributed to a rumour monger named as WJM47196
  • The part "would appear in a series of Radeon RX-600-branded graphics cards" (only the browser title, meta description and URL of the page read "Radeon RX-680 graphics cards"; the on-page headline and the body use RX-600)
  • Mid-range Navi-based cards are said to follow in the first quarter of 2019, with top-of-the-range HBM2 parts after them; Navi is "slated to succeed the Vega architecture", will use a 7nm process and be primarily aimed at next-generation consoles such as the PlayStation 5, "which is expected to be launched before the end of 2020"
  • The Polaris refresh plus mid-range-first Navi "will therefore leave AMD with three graphics card architectures for low-, mid-range and high-end", at a time when Vega is typically only in cards from GBP 450 upwards and 8GB Polaris cards "can be had for under GBP 300"; Nvidia's Turing-based GPUs "could make their debut next month"
  • The article hedges throughout that this is a rumour: the real performance boost "will likely come with HBM2 sporting Navi GPUs or a 7nm Vega 20 GPU with HBM2 aimed at gamers, if WJM47196 is correct"; posted by the V3 Newsdesk on 04 July 2018
  • The Polaris 30 part launched on 15 November 2018 as the Radeon RX 590, at an MSRP of $279; AMD shipped no reference design, and custom cards from XFX, PowerColor, Sapphire and Asus were available on day one

Notable features

  • Claimed specification: a 15 per cent performance boost over the current RX-500 series cards, "which were a minor refresh on 2016's RX-400s", manufactured on the 12-nanometre FinFET process
  • As launched, the RX 590 is another Polaris 10 revision built on GlobalFoundries' 12nm process, with no architectural changes and the same die size and transistor count; it is pin-compatible with Polaris 10, so partners reuse RX 580 board designs
  • Specifications: 2304 stream processors, 1469MHz base and 1545MHz boost clocks, 8GB of 8 Gbps GDDR5 and 225W typical board power, 75W over the original RX 480
  • AMD aimed it at the performance gap between the RX Vega 56 and the RX 580 8GB and at 1080p gamers on older cards such as the GTX 970 and R9 380, with Nvidia's GeForce GTX 1060 6GB as its main competition

changes.after: Suzhou Zhongnan Center Restarts as a 499-Meter Redesign
changes.before: Suzhou Zhongnan Center - Thornton Tomasetti

changes.after: Located to the west of Jinji Lake, the Suzhou Zhongnan Center was first designed as a 729-meter, 137-story mixed-use tower, but that plan was scrapped in 2019 under China's ban on buildings over 500 meters. Construction of a 499.2-meter, 103-story redesign with hotel, office and residential space began in 2020, then halted in mid-2022, when it had reached ground level, over developer Zhongnan Group's financial difficulties.

changes.after:
• The pin's forecast comes from Peter Zeihan's video "The 2nd Holodomor: A Pending Genocide" (Zeihan on Geopolitics, 24 January 2023), which argues that Russia was gearing up for a second Holodomor by deliberately destroying Ukraine's agricultural production
  • Russia let the Black Sea Grain Initiative lapse on 17 July 2023; by then the deal had moved nearly 33 million tonnes of grain and other food from Ukrainian ports to more than 40 countries, 57% of grain exports going to developing countries, with Egypt fifth by number of shipments in 2022; UN Secretary-General Guterres said the deals had helped cut food prices by over 23 per cent since March 2022 and that the decision "will strike a blow to people in need everywhere"
  • Russia then struck grain storage and loading facilities in Ukraine's Black Sea and Danube ports and warned that ships entering Ukrainian waters could be treated as legitimate targets; a 23 August 2023 drone attack on Izmail destroyed 13,000 tons of grain bound for Egypt and Romania, and Egypt's President el-Sisi joined other African leaders at the July 2023 Russia-Africa Summit in urging Putin to renew the deal
  • The Black Sea did not become a no-go zone: Ukraine opened its own corridor, the container ship Joseph Schulte left Odesa through it on 16 August 2023, and by 31 December 2023 Ukraine had moved 13 million tons by sea on 430 vessels
  • Egypt's annual urban inflation reached a record 38% in September 2023, driven by vegetable prices (up 19.2% on the month after one of the hottest summers on record) and a currency that had lost more than half its value since March 2022, while bread and cereal prices fell 1.3% from August
changes.before:
• September and October, Egypt will have food crisis as Russia kills off Ukraine's Agriculture industry and ability to export through it's ports. Black Sea likely becomes a no-go zone.
  • Dated (unconfirmed) to 2023-09-01.

• The Mumbai-Ahmedabad high-speed rail line is India's first bullet-train corridor: 508 km, 12 stations, built and operated by NHSRCL with Japanese Shinkansen technology (E10 Series / B28 "Vande Bullet") and technology transfer under Make in India
  • Specs: standard gauge, 25 kV AC, ETCS Level 2, operating speed 320 km/h (design 350 km/h), a 353 km viaduct; trains are expected to cover the route in two hours versus 5 h 40 min for the current Vande Bharat
  • Construction began February 2021 after COVID delays; the first section, Surat-Bilimora, is planned to open on 15 August 2027 (then Vapi-Surat), and Railways Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw told the Lok Sabha on 23 July 2025 that the Gujarat section is due by December 2027 and the full corridor by December 2029
  • Railways Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw said on 1-2 January 2026 that the first bullet train would start on Independence Day, 15 August 2027
  • Cost is about Rs 1.1 lakh crore, 81% funded by a JICA loan; Rs 67,486 crore had been spent and 47% of civil works completed by October 2024
  • By September 2026 the corridor had reached 62.16 per cent physical progress with over Rs 90,967 crore spent, and the full corridor was still expected to be completed by December 2029

changes.after:
• Brightline West is a privately run high-speed line under construction along the I-15 median, 218 miles (351 km) from the Las Vegas area to Rancho Cucamonga, with stops at Victor Valley and Hesperia and an average journey of about 2h 10m
  • Revenue service is now planned for late 2029, missing the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics target; as of April 2025 officials anticipated September 2029, and in January 2026 Brightline West told FOX5 the line is scheduled for completion by late 2029
  • Costs are estimated at $21.5 billion (January 2026 disclosure) against $8 billion in 2020; the company requested a $6 billion loan on top of a $3 billion US DOT grant and $2.5 billion of private activity bonds (Newsweek cites at least $12 billion)
  • Groundbreaking was 22 April 2024 in Las Vegas; as of October 2025 major construction was expected in April 2026, and track-laying start is not announced
  • In August 2026 financing was still unresolved: the company remained in due diligence for a $6 billion federal RRIF loan, a $400 million equity contribution originally due 31 March had been extended to 10 September, and a $4 billion bank contribution was still pending; the opening was still given as late 2029
  • Brightline (Fortress Investment Group) acquired XpressWest in 2018 and rebranded it Brightline West in 2020; about 50 million people travel between Los Angeles and Las Vegas annually, 85% by car

changes.after:
• The Francis Scott Key Bridge (I-695, Baltimore) opened 23 March 1977; a steel continuous truss 8,636 ft long with a 1,200 ft main span
  • On 26 March 2024 the container ship MV Dali lost power and struck a support pier, collapsing the main spans; six maintenance workers died and two were rescued, and a mayday call let police halt traffic
  • Replacement plans: in May 2024 officials projected $1.7-1.9 billion and completion in fall 2028; Kiewit was named progressive design-builder in August 2024 with opening "expected in Fall 2028"
  • The 2028 target has since been superseded: on 17 November 2025 the Maryland Transportation Authority raised the estimate to $4.3-5.2 billion with an anticipated open-to-traffic date in late 2030, citing much higher material costs, a larger pier protection system and a main span lengthened to 1,665 ft
  • On 28 April 2026 MDTA dropped Kiewit from Phase 2 construction because its proposal far exceeded the state's independent cost estimates; by August 2026 the state planned to award the main overwater contract in June 2027 and still had "a goal of the end of 2030", now asking for completion "as near to December 31, 2030 as practicable" rather than the 2024 requirement of "no later than October 15, 2028"
  • Funding includes a $350 million Chubb insurance payout, a $101.98 million DOJ settlement with the Dali's owner and manager, and a 100 percent federal Emergency Relief share set by law in December 2024

changes.after:
• The Line is a planned linear city in Neom, Tabuk Province, announced in 2021: originally 170 km long, 500 m high and 200 m wide, car-free and carbon-free, for 9 million people
  • The first phase, lasting until 2030, was to cost SAR 1.2 trillion (about US$320 billion) per the crown prince in 2022
  • By 2025 the project had been substantially scaled down or suspended: the Wall Street Journal reported the first phase would be only 2.4 km long (Saudi officials denied an internal audit's findings), with the aim of completing the first half-mile section in 2034
  • A 2023 draft board presentation reportedly estimated full completion in 2080 at $8.8 trillion
  • On 16 September 2025 the Public Investment Fund suspended work until further notice, and by the end of 2025 no construction was taking place; on 22 May 2026 Semafor reported that NEOM had delayed further work on The Line until at least after 2030 while significantly redesigning its twin mirrored skyscrapers, adding that it was unclear when the redesign would be finished or new funding allocated
  • Earlier (October 2024) Neom's chief investment officer said a 5 km central section targeted 2030 with full 170 km completion in 2045; the Guardian in 2022 cited a first phase running until 2030

changes.after:
• SRL East runs 26 km from Cheltenham to Box Hill with 6 stations; work began in 2022 and the planned opening is 2035, as the pin says
  • As of September 2026 six SRL East stations are under construction and tunnel boring began in September 2026, first from Burwood towards Glen Waverley
  • SRL East and SRL North (Box Hill to Melbourne Airport, 34 km, 7 stations) together form a 60 km fully automated underground orbital line with 13 stations connecting eight existing rail lines and three university campuses; SRL West is undefined with no timeframe; the 90 km figure in the pin's description is the full orbital line as Daniel Andrews first announced it on 28 August 2018, connecting 10 existing rail lines at an estimated $50 billion
  • SRL North's date is given two ways on the same page: 2043 in the infobox, while the text says construction is not expected before the 2030s, completion by 2053, and the section may be split in two
  • The links disagree on cost: estimates $31-58 billion for the line, while, The B1M's video "Australia is Building a $125BN Mega-Railway" (published 2023-10-18), carries $125BN only as a title figure for Melbourne's whole metro upgrade - its chapters cover both the Suburban Rail Loop and the Metro Tunnel - and gives no breakdown; the pin applies that $125BN to the loop alone
  • Delivery: owner VicTrack, operator TransitLinX (John Holland and RATP Dev), 4-car driverless Alstom Metropolis trains, Alstom Urbalis Forward signalling and 25 kV AC; the first $3.6 billion tunnel contract was signed in December 2023 with Suburban Connect
  • The project is contested: announced by the Andrews Labor government before the 2018 state election and criticised over political motives, business-case transparency, prioritisation and cost; Coalition leaders Brad Battin (Jan 2025) and then Jess Wilson (from November 2025) pledged to halt it if elected in 2026, and the federal Coalition vowed to scrap $2.2 billion in federal funding before the 2025 election, which it lost
  • It answers Melbourne's radial rail network after earlier orbital attempts failed - the Outer Circle (1888-1891, closed by 1897) and the Inner Circle (opened 1888, closed to passengers 1941) - followed by the road-based M80 Ring Road and EastLink

changes.after:
• Samsung Thailand's newsroom roadmap sets 28 September 2026 as the start of the One UI 9 rollout for the Galaxy S25 series and the Galaxy Z Fold7 and Z Flip7
  • The Galaxy S25 line covered includes the S25, S25+, S25 Ultra, S25 Edge and S25 FE
  • This follows the stable One UI 9 debut in South Korea on 16 September 2026 with the Galaxy S26, S26+ and S26 Ultra, after the software first shipped on the Galaxy Z Fold8 Ultra, Fold8 and Flip8 and out of the box on the Galaxy S26 FE
  • Samsung's global press release gave no rollout dates for older phones, only noting the models that would receive the Privacy Alerts feature, which makes the Thai posting the clearest official indication of plans beyond the S26 series
  • Samsung Thailand originally listed 21 September for the Galaxy S26 series, then moved that date to 28 September so the S26 lines up with the S25 and Z7 foldables - a week's extra wait
  • Sammy Fans reported on 22 September 2026 that the Thai page later dropped a fixed date altogether in favour of "Within September", which the site framed as a change to the announcement timing rather than a confirmed delay of the update itself
  • Older devices remain unscheduled: the press release said One UI 9 would reach the Galaxy S23 FE "by October", later softened by Samsung to later this year, while the Galaxy S24 and S23 series go unmentioned
  • Both SamMobile and Android Authority caution the dates may apply only to Thailand and could be tentative, with exact timing varying by country and carrier; Samsung's US announcement covered only the 16 September S26 start and Canada's cited 21 September
  • The Galaxy S22 series has already had its final major update (Android 16 / One UI 8) but continues to get quarterly security patches
  • In the event's wake, Samsung began the global stable rollout for the Galaxy S26 series in the US on 23 September 2026, prioritising Beta 7 participants, and said it plans to upgrade all eligible devices by the end of the year

Notable features

  • One UI 9 is Samsung's Android 17-based interface release, tested through a beta programme running since May 2026 with seven major beta builds for the Galaxy S26 series, and positioned as the foundation for a later One UI 9.5 upgrade
  • My FanCam automatically tracks a chosen person in a recorded video and keeps them centred, reframing the footage as the scene moves; it requires a Samsung Account and is not supported when there is no subject to track
  • Now Brief gains Generative and Editable Cards so users can build their own daily-summary cards across health, weather and video
  • Now Nudge surfaces context-aware suggestions in the flow of use, such as pulling up reservation details or saving a shared location from a conversation, working with Samsung Messages, Google Messages and Google Chat
  • Creative Studio suggests image-generation prompts tied to upcoming events such as a friend's birthday
  • Interpreter adds a Thread View for reviewing earlier exchanges, with faster Conversation Mode translation and quicker playback on compatible Galaxy Buds
  • Document Scan handles curved book pages and folded corners with less manual correction, adds large-screen-optimised views and an improved Finger Eraser; Voice Recorder structures summaries with headings and tables
  • Security and privacy additions: a Security Brief inside Now Brief flagging malware, unknown-source apps and unnecessary permissions; on-device AI Privacy Alerts; and Scam Detection expanding to Japan, Canada and India
  • Privacy Alerts support spans the Galaxy S26/S25/S24/S23 families (including FE models), Z Fold8 Ultra/Fold8/Flip8 down to Fold5/Flip5, and Tab S11, S10 and S9 tablets
  • Warranty and Care moves device support into Settings, covering warranty checks across linked devices, self-diagnostics, repair estimates and Samsung Care+ management or service booking, with availability varying by region
